spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** **Observability-Driven Testing (ODT)** turns OpenTelemetry traces, spans, and structured events into first-class test assertions.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts End-to-End W3C traceparent Propagation Across Async Queues (Test Runner -> Order API -> Kafka Broker -> Billing Worker -> Tempo / Jaeger); Telemetry-Gated Canary Rollout State Machine (CANARY 5% -> PROMOTED 100% -> AUTO ROLLBACK).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Balance real integration fidelity against CI speed and trace ingest cost. In production progressive delivery (Argo Rollouts / Flagger), automated canary analysis queries Prometheus/Tempo SLIs segmented by `version=canary` vs `version=baseline`—promoting.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore distributed tracing correlation IDs, tail-based sampling, and unbiased canary evaluation.

learningJourney.title: What is Observability-Driven Testing (ODT)
learningJourney.explanation:
**Observability-Driven Testing (ODT)** turns OpenTelemetry traces, spans, and structured events into first-class test assertions.

By injecting W3C **`traceparent`** and **`baggage: test_run_id=...`** headers from test runners (Playwright, pytest, JUnit) into services and Kafka/SQS queues, each test run produces one unified distributed trace—allowing tools like Tracetest or Malabi to assert `span('payment.charge').attributes['retry_count'] == 0` or `db.query_count <= 5`.

sectionDiagram.summary: Trace assertions catch hidden N+1 queries, dropped async events, and silent retries that HTTP 200 hides.

learningJourney.title: Why black-box HTTP 200 assertions miss silent partial failures
learningJourney.explanation:
A black-box `assert response.status_code == 200` passes even when a background Kafka event was dropped, a cache stampede occurred, or an N+1 SQL regression doubled p99 latency.

Two common pitfalls break ODT setups: **Broken Async Context Propagation** (a Kafka/SQS producer omits `traceparent`, orphaning child spans) and **BatchSpanProcessor Flush Races** (the test queries Tempo 100 ms after HTTP 200, before the default 5-second batch flush runs).

ideas.title: Shorten Test Flush Delay
ideas.description: Set `OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY=500` in CI/test environments and poll the trace backend with backoff.

ideas.title: Isolate Synthetic Traffic
ideas.description: Tag synthetic tests with `baggage: test_run_id=...` so they never pollute production SLO error budgets.

learningJourney.title: Asserting on Distributed Trace Spans in CI
learningJourney.explanation: Configure head/tail sampling to retain 100% of traces carrying `test_run_id`, then assert on span existence, error status, and SQL query counts.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```yaml
# Tracetest-style assertion against a distributed Order -> Kafka -> Billing trace
type: Test
spec:
  trigger:
    type: http
    httpRequest: { url: "http://api:8080/v1/orders", method: "POST" }
  specs:
    - selector: span[name="kafka.consume orders"]
      assertions:
        - attr:otel.status_code != "ERROR"
    - selector: span[db.system="postgresql"]
      assertions:
        - attr:tracetest.selected_spans.count <= 5  # Catch N+1 SQL regressions
```

learningJourney.explanation: Balance real integration fidelity against CI speed and trace ingest cost.

benefits: Tests real serialization, SQL plans, headers, and async broker handoffs with zero mock drift.
costs: Seconds per test vs. milliseconds for mocked unit tests.

benefits: Captures 100% of CI/canary test spans without blowing up production ingest quotas.
costs: Requires OTel Collector tail-sampling / attribute-routing rules.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why might a trace-based integration test fail to find expected spans when querying Jaeger/Tempo 100 ms after an HTTP 200 response?

options.text: HTTP 200 responses do not generate OpenTelemetry spans
The service's BatchSpanProcessor buffers spans for a default flush interval (e.g., 5 seconds), creating an async flush race unless OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY is lowered and the test polls with backoff
options.feedback: Correct: lower the flush delay in test environments and poll the trace backend with backoff.

options.text: W3C traceparent headers cannot be used in integration tests
options.feedback: Test runners inject traceparent headers specifically to correlate the test trace.

_recommendedProblem.title: Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
